message.content:
**Summary**

I researched Apple's most recent reported results and placed a buy order. Per Apple's newsroom release (Oct 31, 2024) and its FY2024 Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR, Apple's fiscal Q4 (ended Sept 28, 2024) revenue was **$94.9B, up 6% year over year**, and full-year FY2024 net sales were **$391,035M** (vs $383,285M prior year) with **operating income of $123,216M** and **net income of $93,736M**, or **$6.08 diluted EPS** — down slightly from $6.13 a year earlier primarily because of a **one-time $10.2B income tax charge**. So the trend is modest top-line reacceleration and strong operating profitability, with the EPS dip being an accounting/tax item rather than operating deterioration. Coverage on near-term iPhone 16 and Apple Intelligence demand was thin in the sources I found (only a brief note that shares were "little changed at about $222" as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout), so I treated that as neutral color rather than a strong signal. With AAPL quoted at **$222.70** (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I bought **44 shares with a limit order at $223.00**, which filled at $223.00 for roughly **$9,812** — inside the $10,000 per-order cap, well inside the $20,000 daily cap, and within about 0.13% of the market price; no funds were moved out of the account, and no MSFT or sell activity was involved.

One caveat worth flagging: the specific segment splits (iPhone vs. Services vs. Greater China) weren't available in the pages I could retrieve, so my decision rests on the headline consolidated figures above rather than segment detail.
